_comment: Worked example: adaptive biomarker-ENRICHMENT Phase 2 trial with a time-to-event primary endpoint (PFS), modeled on an EGFR-mutant NSCLC setting. Full population H_F + biomarker-positive subgroup H_S, one interim analysis with adaptive enrichment + non-binding futility, closed test for multiplicity. Disease-specific numbers are ILLUSTRATIVE assumptions, not real data.

report.title: Adaptive Biomarker-Enrichment Trial (NSCLC / EGFR example)
report.subtitle: Time-to-event endpoint | population enrichment | group-sequential
report.recommendation: Fit for purpose when the biomarker-positive subgroup is expected to carry most of the treatment effect; confirm the assumed prevalence and the enrichment decision rule with clinical and translational leads before finalizing sample size.
references: Simon N, Simon R. Adaptive enrichment designs for clinical trials. Biostatistics 2013;14(4):613-625.
Wang SJ, Hung HMJ, O'Neill RT. Adaptive patient enrichment designs in therapeutic trials. Biometrical Journal 2009;51(2):358-374.
Jenkins M, Stone A, Jennison C. An adaptive seamless phase II/III design. Pharmaceutical Statistics 2011;10(4):347-356.
Wassmer G, Pahlke F. rpact: Confirmatory Adaptive Clinical Trial Design and Analysis. R package.
